learning_outcomes.text: Introduce innovative sensors based on smart materials, capable of coupling different physical quantities (mechanical, electromagnetic, thermal, etc.) within their constitutive relations.
Understand multifunctional materials for actuation, sensing, and energy conversion, combining efficiency and speed in precision applications or harsh environments.
Provide an introduction to energy harvesting as the future technique for powering wireless sensors.
Introduce smart materials (e.g., photovoltaic, magnetostrictive, piezoelectric, magnetothermal, etc.).
Apply a problem-solving methodology, presenting methods and concepts as solutions to practical application challenges.

syllabus_topics: Smart Sensors: general characteristics and applications (IoT, biomedical, etc.)
Multifunctional materials and macro/mesoscopic description of phenomena (magnetostriction, piezoelectricity, etc.)
Energy Harvesting: general characteristics and applications
Devices for energy harvesting (photovoltaic panels, vibrational harvesters, etc.)
Laboratory Sessions: hands-on activities on smart sensors and energy harvesting devices

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam, focused on course topics and project discussion

assessment_rules: The exam is based on the preparation of a short project to be submitted before the exam and an oral part focused on the topics covered in the course syllabus and on the discussion of the short project.
bibliography: Jacob Fraden, Handbook of Modern Sensors; Physics, Designs, and Applications, Springer (available in pdf)
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Elettronica E Biomedica (Electronics And Biomedical Engineering), classe L-8 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria dell'informazione
